name: Text messaging (SMS)
how: Mobile phone, digital cellular signalling channel, store-and-forward message centre
impact: Became the first mass digital messaging habit, trillions of texts a year by the 2000s and still the fallback channel for billions.

name: Digital cellular network (2G)
how: Mobile phone, microchips, SIM smart card, digital speech compression; ★ time-division multiplexing of radio channels
impact: Digital, cheap, roaming networks carried mobile phones from executives to over a billion people by 2002.
why: A version of Mobile phone (1983), but going digital is what made phones cheap and global and enabled texting, so m4 says borderline.

name: Home broadband (DSL and cable modem)
how: Copper phone line or TV cable, modem, microchips; ★ splitting one wire into many narrow frequency bands (discrete multitone)
impact: Turned the internet from a dial-up chore into an always-on utility for over a billion households.

name: Open-source operating system
how: Personal computer, compilers, the Internet for distributed volunteer development
impact: Runs most of the world's servers, cloud data centres, supercomputers and every Android phone.

name: Universal serial port (USB)
how: Insulated wire & cable, microchips, standard plug; ★ device announces itself to the host (plug and play)
impact: A single connector standard in tens of billions of devices, also the default way to charge small electronics.

name: Conjugate vaccines
how: Bacterial sugar coat chemically bonded to a carrier protein; ★ protein carrier makes infants' immune systems respond to sugars
impact: Hib and later pneumococcal conjugate vaccines prevent hundreds of thousands of child deaths from meningitis and pneumonia every year.

name: Graphics processor (GPU)
how: Microchips, memory chip; ★ thousands of identical arithmetic units working in parallel
impact: Draws every screen in games and phones and became the engine that deep learning and large language models run on.

name: Secure web connection (SSL/TLS)
how: Public-key encryption, certificate authorities, the Web
impact: Protects nearly every web page, payment and login, the padlock behind online shopping and banking.
why: It is public-key encryption put onto the web; it changed who uses encryption (everyone, daily), so m4 says borderline.

name: Pay-per-click online advertising
how: Search engine, auctions run by software, click tracking
impact: Funds the free search, email, video and social media used by billions; the biggest share of all advertising spending.
why: Is it an invention or a business model? It is how the free internet is paid for.

name: CMOS camera chip
how: Microchips, photodiode in each pixel with its own amplifier; photoelectric effect
impact: The camera in every phone, car and laptop, billions made each year.
why: A cheaper, lower-power version of CCD image sensor (1969); it put cameras into every phone, so borderline.

name: Electronic stability control
how: Anti-lock brakes, gyroscope yaw sensor, microchips, braking individual wheels
impact: Mandatory on new cars in the US and EU; estimated to cut fatal single-car crashes by about a third.

name: MEMS motion sensors
how: Microchips, silicon etched into tiny springs and masses; ★ capacitance changes as a microscopic mass moves
impact: Every phone, airbag, game controller and drone senses motion and tilt with these, billions a year.

name: Online banking
how: The Web, secure web connection, bank databases
impact: Most bank customers in rich countries and hundreds of millions in Asia now bank mainly online or by phone.

name: Instant messaging
how: The Internet, presence server, personal computer
impact: Grew into the chat apps used by about three billion people daily.
why: Close to Email and Social media already kept, and its biggest use came later on smartphones.

name: Flat-screen display (thin-film-transistor LCD)
how: Liquid crystal display, a transistor printed behind every pixel on glass
impact: Flat colour screens replaced the cathode-ray tube in every laptop, monitor and TV.
why: A version of Liquid crystal display (1968), but the per-pixel transistor made big colour flat screens possible, so borderline.

name: OLED display
how: Thin organic films, transparent electrodes, thin-film transistors; ★ electroluminescence of organic molecules
impact: The screen in most smartphones and premium TVs, over a billion made each year.
why: First sold in 1997 (a car stereo) but only widely used from about 2010 in phones.

name: Internet telephony (VoIP)
how: The Internet, compressed media, microchips
impact: Carries most of the world's phone and video calls today.
why: Same job as the telephone and close to Video calling (2003) already kept.

name: Fibre-optic amplifiers and wavelength multiplexing
how: Fiber optics, laser diodes, erbium-doped fibre; ★ optical amplification by stimulated emission in a doped fibre
impact: Multiplied each fibre's capacity a hundredfold; carries nearly all intercontinental internet traffic.
why: An upgrade to Fiber optic communication (1977) that nobody sees, though the internet's backbone runs on it.

name: DVD
how: Laser, laser disks, compressed media, red laser diode
impact: Over a billion players sold; the standard way to own and rent films until streaming.
why: A shrunk, denser Laser disk (1972) doing the same job, but it was the first one most households used.

name: Electric bicycle
how: Bicycle, electric motor, battery, torque sensor
impact: Around 300 million in China alone; the main motor vehicle for many Asian commuters.
why: A bicycle with a motor; it changed who can ride (older, longer, hillier trips), so borderline.

name: QR code
how: Barcode, camera chip, error-correcting code; ★ 2D pattern readable from any angle
impact: Scanned by billions of phones for payments, menus and tickets, especially in China and India.
why: A version of Barcode scanner (1974); invented in 1994 but mass use came with phone cameras after 2010.

name: Online maps and directions
how: The Web, digitised street maps, route-finding software (shortest-path search)
impact: Billions of people find their way with phone maps daily; it replaced the paper road atlas.
why: You dropped Car satnav (1995); this is its web/phone cousin, which is in far more daily use.

name: Unicode text encoding
how: Character tables, software standards
impact: Lets every language on earth be typed, stored and sent on every computer and phone.
why: Is a standard an invention? Every text you read on a screen runs on it.

name: Recommendation algorithms
how: Databases, statistics of what similar people chose, the Web
impact: Choose much of what billions of people watch, read and buy.
why: An algorithm rather than a device, and mostly a piece of shopping, streaming and social media.

name: Digital satellite and terrestrial TV
how: Communications satellites, compressed media, dish antenna, set-top box
impact: Hundreds of millions of homes, e.g. most of India's TV households, watch through digital dishes.
why: A version of Television and communications satellites; compression made hundreds of channels cheap.

name: Real-time PCR testing
how: PCR, fluorescent dye probes, photocell; ★ fluorescence that grows with each copying cycle
impact: The standard lab test for infections, from HIV viral load to the billions of COVID-19 tests.
why: A version of PCR (1983) kept; reading the result live made it a routine clinical test.

name: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)
how: Test-tube baby methods, microscope, glass micro-needle
impact: Used in most IVF cycles worldwide; millions of children born.
why: A version of Test-tube baby (1978) that made male infertility treatable.

name: Neonicotinoid insecticides
how: Synthetic chemistry, seed coating; ★ chemical that jams insects' nerve receptors
impact: The world's most used insecticide class, coating most maize, soy and rape seed; also blamed for harming bees.
why: Standard in farming, but you dropped Glyphosate weedkiller, so it may also go.

name: Erectile dysfunction pills
how: Synthetic drug blocking an enzyme (PDE5) that relaxes blood vessels
impact: Prescribed to tens of millions of men; now cheap generics.
why: Near the cut: widely used, but its impact is personal rather than world-changing.

name: Spiral CT scanner
how: CAT scan, slip-ring rotating gantry, moving table
impact: Made CT fast enough to be routine; hundreds of millions of scans a year.
why: A faster CAT scan (1972); it changed how widely CT is used, so borderline.

name: GPS-guided bomb
how: Precision-guided bombs, GPS receiver, fins
impact: Made precision strikes cheap and all-weather; the default air weapon since 1999.
why: A version of Precision-guided bombs (1972) kept; GPS made it cheap and usable in any weather.

name: Giant-magnetoresistance disk head
how: Hard disk drive; ★ giant magnetoresistance (resistance of thin magnetic layers swings with field)
impact: Let hard drives grow a thousandfold, making cheap mass storage and data centres possible.
why: A version of Hard disk drive (1956); invisible to users but it changed how drives read data.

name: Lung surfactant for premature babies
how: Lung-lining lipids from cattle or synthetic, breathing tube
impact: Cut deaths of very premature babies from breathing failure by roughly a third.
why: Below the decade's cut; important for newborns but used only in hospital neonatal units.

name: Online dating
how: The Web, databases, matching software
impact: Now how the largest share of couples meet in the US and many other countries.
why: Below the decade's cut; a service built on the Web rather than a new assembly.

name: Prepaid mobile phone plans
how: Mobile phone network, top-up vouchers, billing software
impact: Made mobile phones affordable for the poor; most phones in Africa and South Asia are prepaid.
why: Below the decade's cut, and a business model more than an invention.

name: Peer-to-peer file sharing
how: The Internet, compressed media, personal computer
impact: Hit tens of millions of users and forced the music industry onto streaming.
why: Below the decade's cut; its job passed to streaming.

name: Atypical antipsychotics
how: Synthetic drugs blocking dopamine and serotonin receptors
impact: The standard treatment for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
why: Below the decade's cut; an improvement on Tranquilizers (1952).

name: Computer-animated feature films
how: Computer graphics software, render farms of computers
impact: Now how nearly all animated and effects-heavy films are made.
why: Below the decade's cut.

name: Photo-editing software
how: Personal computer, graphical user interface, digital images
impact: The standard tool of photography, design and print.
why: Below the decade's cut.

name: Common-rail diesel injection
how: Diesel engine, high-pressure pump, electronic injectors, microchips
impact: Made diesel cars quiet and frugal; standard in every modern diesel engine.
why: Below the decade's cut, and an engine detail rather than something people handle.

name: Portable document format (PDF)
how: Page description language, personal computer
impact: The default format for forms, papers and contracts.
why: Below the decade's cut.

name: Hormonal IUD
how: Plastic T-frame, slow-release progestin
impact: Used by tens of millions of women.
why: Below the decade's cut; a variant of existing contraception.

name: Animal cloning
how: Nuclear transfer into an emptied egg cell
impact: Used in research and some livestock breeding; a 1990s headline (Dolly the sheep).
why: Still a lab and breeding technique, and Asimov already has Vertebrate clones (1967).
